chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān and Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: An Imam of a people is afflicted with janabah during travel, and he does not have with him enough water for ghusl. Should some of them perform wudu and he lead them in salat? He said: No. Rather, the junub performs tayammum and leads them in salat, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made earth a purifier.

key_terms.التُّرَابَ: earth or soil used for tayammum
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the circumstance in which the ruling is being asked about
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: the person in a state of janabah
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: the ritual bath required after janabah
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: to perform tayammum as a substitute purification

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah who performs tayammum lead people with wudu in salat while traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning an Imam in a state of janabah while traveling without sufficient water for ghusl. It establishes that he should perform tayammum and may then lead those who have wudu in salat, because Allah has made earth a means of ritual purification.
